title: Why pen caps have a hole
pause_note: v5, Why Is It Designed Like That? DO hook: a pen cap held up to the light, a beam through the hole at 0 s; wrong guess (for the ink) stamped out at ~4 s; reveal: the cap is breathed in at ~7 s and air still flows through the hole at ~9 s; standard 8 L/min; or too big to breathe in; loop back to the cap in the light; one-word question.

beats: Hold a pen cap up to the light. See the hole?
It's not there for the ink.
Kids chew caps, and now and then, one gets breathed in.
Stuck in the windpipe, the hole still lets air through, until a doctor gets it out.
A safety standard asks for at least eight litres of air a minute through the cap.
Or a cap too big to breathe in at all.
